Comments:
This letter is well organisaed (Organisation and Layout: 6) and has appropriate and formal language with correct register and tone (Genre and Style: 6). Unfortunately, there are  number of grammar issues that make paragraph 4 diffiuclt to understand. The poor grammer means Language is 3/7 but it also affect clearness (Conciseness and Clarity). Another problem is that some key detail is not in the letter. I will explain further about all these issues below. 

In this paragraph the patient visited ‘today’. I understand that this is an event which is finished. But his symtpoms, presumably, are still true? So you need to say “He is still in pain”

Another tense issue. You need to say “he is revovering well” because this is an incomplete process. He hasn’t fully recovered yet. 
Again “He is experiences pain after 30 minutes” (Present Simple) or “He is experiencing pain after 30 minutes” (Present Contiuous) are the tenses you need here. 
There is another problem with the modal auxiliary verb ‘would’. You need ‘can’ not ‘would’. 

There is another issue with time in paragraph2:


You cannot say ‘ago’ here. ‘Ago’ means from now to a past time. ‘I started teaching OET 4 years ago’. You cannot strt on a day that is already past (21/03/15) and use ago because ‘ago’ has the idea of the past until now. 
Also this:


You can only use the word ‘since’ with Present Perfect. 
When ‘since’ means ‘starting point’. 

There is another meaning of since which is ‘because’. In that case you can use past simple. 

Another issue is ‘considering’:



You cannot use this word like this. You need ‘Regarding his…’. 

Finally what didn’t you mention this case note:



He is walking 30 minutes every day which is a positive thing, although he finds it tiring. Have I missed it in the letter? I cant see it. 


Grade:
C
